paragraph: [In late July 2025 the analyst Darwin Costa told Portal de TI that Angonix peaked at 59.5 Gbps](<https://pti.ao/trafego-de-internet-em-angola-atinge-maximos-historicos/>), and that Microsoft and Meta were present at Angola's exchanges. In the last twelve months, [the Internet Society's IXP Tracker listed the Angola Internet Exchange Point (Angonix) in Luanda as active with 23 members in June 2026](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/ixp-tracker/country/AO/>). [In November 2025 the same analyst said Angola's two active exchanges were both in Luanda](<https://pti.ao/internet-em-angola-especialista-defende-descentralizacao-da-internet-em-angola/>). No source found gives the exchange's traffic at two dates a year apart. Operating would need traffic figures at two dates a year or more apart, the later higher.

[The Internet Society's IXP Tracker lists Akamai Technologies (AS20940, 1 Gbps) and Meta (AS63293, 10 Gbps) as members of BDIXP in Bujumbura, from PeeringDB data of August 2026](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/ixp-tracker/ixp/706/>). The Tracker lists 9 member ASNs and 26 Gbps of cumulative port capacity. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found gives the exchange's traffic at two dates a year apart, and none names a second city or networks from other countries. Operating would need traffic figures at two dates a year or more apart, the later higher.

[Internet Society Pulse, from PeeringDB data last updated January 2026, lists BENIN-IX in Cotonou with 4 member networks](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/ixp-tracker/ixp/395/>). [The Internet Society says the technical community completed deployment of the Cotonou Internet Exchange (COTIX) at the end of 2024, launching with four members](<https://www.internetsociety.org/blog/2026/07/how-local-peering-is-strengthening-africas-internet/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network such as Google, Meta, Akamai, Netflix or Cloudflare has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[In May 2026 the Internet Society said traffic at BFIX reached 6 Gbps at peak, up from 0.5 Gbps before its support from 2019](<https://www.internetsociety.org/blog/2026/05/local-infrastructure-lower-costs-how-peering-is-moving-the-needle-on-internet-affordability/>). The same source says 80% of Burkina Faso's networks are IXP members or customers of IXP members, citing Internet Society Pulse data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at BFIX or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[In October 2025 the regulator BOCRA said the Botswana Internet Exchange, BINX, hosts a Google Cache Cluster](<http://www.bocra.org.bw/sites/default/files/sites/default/files/documents/BOCRA_Newsletter%2C_Issue_003_compressed.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [PeeringDB showed BoFiNet's new Digital Delta IX in Gaborone with one peer, BoFiNet itself, in April 2026](<https://www.peeringdb.com/ix/5002>). [BoFiNet launched it for operators, content and cloud providers in October 2026](<https://itweb.africa/article/bofinet-launches-digital-delta-ixp/8OKdWMDXL9VMbznQ>). No source found gives either exchange's traffic at two dates a year apart. Packet Clearing House's 2025 directory lists BINX as defunct, against BOCRA's account. Operating would need traffic figures at two dates a year or more apart, the later higher.

[ARTCI says CIVIX, the national exchange point, has been in service since October 2013](<https://fr.apanews.net/technologies/peering-day-2026-la-rci-vise-des-ports-internet-de-100-gbps/>). [In May 2024 ARTCI said the Netflix cache was hosted there](<https://www.fratel.org/documents/2024/05/8.-TR2-ARTCI.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [in June 2026 ARTCI said Akamai had joined CIVIX and gave average daily traffic of 20 Gbps for 2020 to 2024 and 36 Gbps for 2025 to 2026](<https://fr.apanews.net/technologies/peering-day-2026-la-rci-vise-des-ports-internet-de-100-gbps/>). [The third point of presence, announced in August 2025, is at Grand-Bassam](<https://www.fratmat.info/article/2635918/economie/forum-sur-le-peering-en-cote-divoire-lartci-impulse-une-dynamique-nouvelle-pour-linterconnexion-locale>), a resort beside Abidjan. No second city and no operators from other countries have been found. Mature would need the exchange to reach beyond one city, through a second exchange or point of presence in another city, or operators from other countries peering there.

[In August 2026 Internet Society Pulse, from PeeringDB, listed 10 member networks and 40 Gbps of port capacity at CAMIX in Douala](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/ixp-tracker/ixp/704/>). [Pulse lists Akamai as a member with a 4 Gbps port](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/ixp-tracker/ixp/704/>). [In July 2025 Camtel staff said CAMIX brings several players together but is still embryonic](<https://www.digitalbusiness.africa/cameroun-camtel-projette-de-creer-9-datacenters-decentralises-pour-les-prochaines-annees/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found gives the exchange's traffic at two dates a year apart. Operating would need traffic figures at two dates a year or more apart, the later higher.

[ISPA-DRC built the Kinshasa Internet Exchange (KINIX) in November 2012](<https://www.internetsociety.org/blog/2024/02/the-decade-that-changed-the-democratic-republic-of-congos-internet/>). [ISPA-DRC gave KINIX a traffic peak of 84 Gbps in August 2024](<https://www.afpif.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/RDC-Cache-Fill-Strategies.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [in August 2026 Tech Africa said 23 networks took part at KINIX, that Meta and Cloudflare peer there, and that KINIX said it exchanged more than 1 terabit per second](<https://tech.africa/kinix-raxio-kinshasa-exchange/>). [The Internet Society says ISPA-DRC opened exchanges in Lubumbashi in 2019 and Goma in 2021](<https://www.internetsociety.org/blog/2024/02/the-decade-that-changed-the-democratic-republic-of-congos-internet/>). Both traffic figures for KINIX are the operator's own.

[The CGIX portal, run with the regulator ARPCE, reports the Congo internet exchange point in operation with 4 connected members and 1 point of presence](<https://www.cgix.cg/>). Its traffic counter shows 70 Mb/s per hour, which this file reads as 2022 because the portal gives no date. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there, and none names a second city. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[Comores Cables states on its own corporate page that an IXP has been installed at Moroni](<https://www.comorescables.km/Technologies>). The page gives no date, so this file uses its published year, 2026. It says the exchange is there to enable local traffic exchange between Comores Telecom and Yas Comores. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[PCH's Internet Exchange Directory lists CV-IXP (Associação Cabo Verde Internet Exchange Point) in Praia as an Active Ethernet exchange established 29 November 2022](<https://www.pch.net/ixp/details/2324>). [PeeringDB lists CV-IXP in Praia with 5 peers, 6 connections and 23G total capacity](<https://www.peeringdb.com/ix/4037>), in a record dated 2024. [The Cabo Verde government's own status booklet states that it has introduced the IXP](<https://www.governo.cv/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/economiadigital.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[On 28 September 2026 Wingu Africa presented to Djibouti's communications minister an internet exchange point already in service within its data centre in Djibouti](<https://www.adi.dj/article/138942>). [Wingu Africa says it launched the AMS-IX Djibouti Internet exchange, expanding on DjIX](<https://www.connectingafrica.com/data-centers/wingu-africa-secures-60m-to-fuel-east-african-expansion>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. The September 2026 report describes an exchange already in service. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[AMS-IX says EG-IX opened in Cairo with Telecom Egypt in April 2022](<https://www.ams-ix.net/ams/news/eg-ix-strengthening-regional-connectivity-from-cairo>). It gives a peak of 89 Gb/s in 2023 and 338 Gb/s in 2025. In the last twelve months, [AMS-IX gave a peak of 945 Gb/s by the third quarter of 2026, with 19 networks connected](<https://www.ams-ix.net/ams/news/eg-ix-strengthening-regional-connectivity-from-cairo>). [The African IXP Association also lists Cairo IX (CAIX), opened in 2002, in Cairo](<https://af-ix.org/ixps-list>). [In September 2026 Tech Africa listed Meta, Amazon and Microsoft among the members, and said two Jordanian carriers were members at EG-IX in Cairo](<https://tech.africa/eg-ix-cairo-18-members/>).

[In 2026 the Internet Society's Pulse IXP Tracker stated there are no active internet exchange points in Eritrea](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/ixp-tracker/country/ER/>), and none listed in PeeringDB with three or more member ASNs. Nothing dated later names one in service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found shows networks handing each other traffic directly at an exchange point, whoever runs it. Preparing would need an exchange point in service, where networks hand each other traffic directly, whoever runs it.

[Internet Society Pulse, from self-reported PeeringDB data last updated January 2026, lists ADDIX in Addis Ababa with 3 members](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/ixp-tracker/ixp/1339/>). [Wingu Africa states that ADDIX, Ethiopia's first IXP, launched over a year before 4 September 2025](<https://www.wingu.africa/latest-news/transforming-connectivity-ethiopias-first-internet-exchange-hosted-at-wingu-africa>). It is operated by ADDIX Technology Solutions and hosted at Wingu's data centre in the ICT Park. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[ISOC Pulse IXP Tracker, from PeeringDB data, lists 1 active IXP in Gabon with 8 combined members as of September 2026](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/ixp-tracker/country/GA/>). In the last twelve months, GabonReview reported in May 2026 that [GABIX, created in 2014, was relaunched](<https://www.gabonreview.com/souverainete-numerique-le-gabon-relance-gabix-son-point-dechange-internet-local/>). Gabon Telecom and Airtel Gabon reconnected, joining ANINF and CanalBox/GVA, the two that had kept activity since 2019. It put local traffic at over 250 Mbps. No source found says a global content network has a cache at GABIX or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[Google and Akamai connect at GIXA in Accra, per bgp.tools and PeeringDB data of 10 August 2026; Meta is also present there](<https://tech.africa/accra-three-internet-exchanges/>). [The operator announced 200 Gbps of aggregate traffic at Accra-IX on 10 August 2026, against 525 Gbps of connected ports](<https://tech.africa/accra-three-internet-exchanges/>). The article notes that no public traffic graph exists. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and only one traffic reading has been found. No source found gives the exchange's traffic at two dates a year apart. Operating would need traffic figures at two dates a year or more apart, the later higher.

[The Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy (MPTEN) lists among its 2025 achievements an operational Internet exchange point (IXP) in Guinea](<https://www.africaguinee.com/app/uploads/2026/01/Realisations_MPTEN_2025_compressed.pdf>), which lets Guinean operators exchange traffic directly without going through abroad. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names its members, city or traffic. None says a global content network has a cache there or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[The SIXP administrator told AfPIF 2015 that the Serekunda Internet Exchange Point (AS37698), established in July 2014, is the first and only IXP in The Gambia and has seven ASNs peering](<https://www.afpif.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/10/Gambia-IXP-Experience-.pdf>). [The Internet Society reports that SIXP was launched on 12 July 2014 in Banjul with African Union AXIS support](<https://www.internetsociety.org/news/press-releases/2014/first-internet-exchange-point-in-the-gambia-launched-in-banjul/>). The administrator gave a maximum traffic of 50.541 Mbit/s. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[Packet Clearing House's report of 21 August 2026 lists Guinea-Bissau among 51 countries with no internet exchange point, against 162 countries with one or more](<https://www.pch.net/ixp/summary>). Nothing dated later names one in service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found shows networks in Guinea-Bissau handing each other traffic directly at an exchange point, whoever runs it. Preparing would need an exchange point in service, where networks hand each other traffic directly, whoever runs it.

A cloud provider connected to LINX Mombasa in 2025 and to LINX Nairobi in 2026, [as ITWeb Africa reports, citing LINX](<https://itweb.africa/article/linx-expands-kenya-peering-network/5yONP7ErXpRMXWrb>). It lists TikTok among the platforms active on the Nairobi exchange. [The companies say combined traffic across the two Kenyan LINX exchange points rose twentyfold over the past year, to a peak above 330 Gbps](<https://itweb.africa/article/linx-expands-kenya-peering-network/5yONP7ErXpRMXWrb>), with no starting figure given. No change has been found in the last twelve months. [LINX states LINX Mombasa is a second exchange point in service in Kenya alongside LINX Nairobi, the first IXP with a physical presence in both cities](<https://www.linx.net/news/linx-mombasa-ready-for-business/>).

[The African Union Commission and Liberia's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications officially launched the Liberian Internet Exchange Point (LIXP) in Monrovia on 6 August 2015](<https://au.int/en/newsevents/20150802/setting-and-launching-internet-exchange-point-liberia>). [LTA Commissioner Angela Cassell Bush said Liberia's IXP, hosted by the Cable Consortium of Liberia, remains functional](<https://lta.gov.lr/lta-highlights-need-to-strengthen-liberias-internet-exchange-point-atnational-peering-forum/>), though many ISPs are not yet peering there. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[Packet Clearing House's report of 21 August 2026 lists Libya among 51 countries without an internet exchange point, against 162 countries with one or more](<https://www.pch.net/ixp/summary>). [PeeringDB's record for Tripoli IXP shows 0 peers, 0 connections and an empty peer table, last updated 2024-04-25 and served in that state on 2026-09-03](<https://www.peeringdb.com/ix/4450>). Nothing dated later names an exchange in service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need an exchange point in service, where networks hand each other traffic directly, whoever runs it.

[In May 2026 PeeringDB listed the Lesotho Internet Exchange Point (LIXP) in Maseru with three peers](<https://www.peeringdb.com/ix/5015>), Econet Telecom Lesotho among them. In the last twelve months, [LIXP was relaunched after a revamp in February 2026](<https://www.thereporter.co.ls/2026/02/02/lesotho-revamps-internet-exchange-infrastructure/>). It had been [founded in 2011, stopped, and resumed in 2016](<https://www.thereporter.co.ls/2026/02/02/lesotho-revamps-internet-exchange-infrastructure/>). [The Lesotho Communications Authority says it serves five ISPs and two content delivery networks](<https://www.thereporter.co.ls/2026/02/02/lesotho-revamps-internet-exchange-infrastructure/>), without naming them. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[The Internet Society's IXP Tracker lists the Casablanca Internet Exchange Point (CAS-IX) with 3 members and 30 Gbps of aggregate capacity, with data as of May 2026](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/fr/ixp-tracker/ixp/760/>). [It lists FEZIX in Fez with 3 Moroccan members and 210 Gbps, on PeeringDB data of January 2026](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/fr/ixp-tracker/ixp/849/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at either exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[Internet Society Pulse lists one active IXP in Madagascar, MGIX in Antananarivo, with 4 members as of February 2026](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/ixp-tracker/country/MG/>). In the last twelve months, [the Internet Society said in July 2026 that Madagascar has revived MGIX](<https://www.internetsociety.org/blog/2026/07/how-local-peering-is-strengthening-africas-internet/>). [Its Foundation's grant record says MGIX, Madagascar's first IXP, had been suspended since 2019](<https://www.isocfoundation.org/2025/01/meet-the-new-grantees-improving-peering-and-interconnection-around-the-globe/>). A 2024 grant of USD 49,958 to iRENALA is to restart it. No source found says a global content network has a cache at MGIX or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[The ECOWAS SIGTEL regional inventory, read in 2026, lists one Internet Exchange Point in Mali, Mali IX (MLIX) in Bamako, among 14 in the ECOWAS member states](<https://sigtel.ecowas.int/regional-fiber-infrastructure/>). The inventory gives no member count or traffic. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there, and none names a second city. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[MOZIX, the Mozambique Internet Exchange in Maputo, says it was created in May 2002 and now has 18 peers](<https://mozix.org.mz/>). [In May 2025 CIUEM's director called MozIX the only internet exchange point in the country](<https://www.ciuem.mz/ciuem-destaca-papel-da-internet-como-espaco-publico-e-inclusivo-no-forum-de-governacao-da-internet-em-mocambique/>). [The same month he put its peak traffic at over 150 Gbps, with 19 peering members](<https://capacityglobal.com/news/mozambique-internet-exchange-launches-new-pop-at-digital-realtys-maputo-data-centre/>). In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: [in August 2026 the communications minister called MozIX the national traffic exchange point](<https://www.diarioeconomico.co.mz/2026/08/03/trends/inovacao/uem-inaugura-centro-de-dados-para-reforcar-transformacao-digital-e-investigacao-cientifica/>). No global content network has been found peering there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[The Ministry of Digital Transformation officially launched the national internet exchange centre at International Mauritanian Telecommunications on 28 May 2025](<https://fr.saharamedias.net/mauritanie-lancement-officiel-du-centre-national-dechange-internet/>). [A feasibility study of June 2014 stated that Mauritania had no exchange point yet, with Dakar in effect acting as the IXP for its operators](<https://mtnima.gov.mr/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Rapport_final-IXP.pdf>). [In August 2025 the ministry called the exchange recently launched](<https://ami.mr/fr/archives/276833>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[Internet Society Pulse, from PeeringDB data of May 2026, lists the Mauritius Internet Exchange Point (MIXP) in Ebene with 19 members and 95 Gbps of cumulative port capacity](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/ixp-tracker/ixp/516/>). [MIXP's own route-server looking glass showed Route Server 1 (IPv6) last reconfigured on 15 June 2026](<https://portal.mixp.org/index.php/lg/rs1-mixp-ipv6>). Five of the members are registered abroad, in the United States, South Africa and Guadeloupe. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[MISPA says the Malawi Internet Exchange (MIX) in Blantyre began operating on 4 December 2008](<http://www.mispa.org.mw/mix.html>). [In April 2024 MISPA's chair said the MIX provides content caches from Google, Facebook and Akamai](<https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-T/Workshops-and-Seminars/2024/0408/Documents/Paulos%20B%20Nyirenda.pdf>). In the last twelve months, [the Internet Society said in July 2026 that the Lilongwe Internet Exchange (LLIX) had launched with five peers](<https://www.internetsociety.org/blog/2026/07/how-local-peering-is-strengthening-africas-internet/>). [A MACRA deck of September 2023 had said Malawi had one exchange, in Blantyre](<https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-T/Workshops-and-Seminars/2023/1004/Documents/Daud%20Elvin%20Suleman.pdf>). No source found gives the MIX's traffic at two dates a year apart. Operating would need traffic figures at two dates a year or more apart, the later higher.

[In 2026 Internet Society Pulse, from PeeringDB, listed the Windhoek Internet Exchange Point (IXP Namibia) with 6 member networks and 23 Gbps of cumulative port capacity](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/ixp-tracker/ixp/368/>). One new member joined in the 12 months before. Pulse also lists Paratus Africa, registered in Mauritius, as a member. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[Agence Ecofin reports that Niger inaugurated a new Internet Exchange Point in Niamey on 19 August 2025, opened by the Minister of Communication and New Information Technologies](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/2108-130856-le-niger-se-dote-d-un-nouveau-point-d-echange-internet>). [ANP, citing the Smart Villages project (PVI), reports the creation of Niger's first Internet Exchange Point with the operator Niger Telecoms](<https://anp.ne/niger-grace-aux-infrastructures-adaptees-fournies-par-le-pvi-plus-de-900-localites-accedent-a-une-connectivite-numerique-haut-debit/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[IXPN, founded in 2006, says it serves more than 130 networks from several Lagos data centres, as of October 2026](<https://techtvnetwork.ng/post/ixpn-at-20-how-nigerias-internet-exchange-point-has-transformed-local-internet-connectivity>). [Google, Meta, Microsoft and TikTok are among its members, per IT Pulse Nigeria in February 2026](<https://itpulse.com.ng/how-local-peering-grew-ixpns-traffic-from-4-gbps-in-2015-to-1-7-tbps-in-2025/>). [Its aggregate peak traffic rose from 4 Gbps in 2015 to 1.7 Tbps in 2025](<https://itpulse.com.ng/how-local-peering-grew-ixpns-traffic-from-4-gbps-in-2015-to-1-7-tbps-in-2025/>). In the last twelve months, [Digital Realty added an IXPN point of presence at its Ibeju-Lekki data centre in Lagos in April 2026](<https://techtvnetwork.ng/post/ixpn-at-20-how-nigerias-internet-exchange-point-has-transformed-local-internet-connectivity>). [In October 2026 IXPN reported regional connectivity in Abuja and Enugu, beside its points of presence in Lagos](<https://techtvnetwork.ng/post/ixpn-at-20-how-nigerias-internet-exchange-point-has-transformed-local-internet-connectivity>).

[In July 2026 the Internet Society said RINEX, the Rwanda Internet Exchange, has become a central part of Rwanda's digital ecosystem](<https://www.internetsociety.org/blog/2026/07/how-local-peering-is-strengthening-africas-internet/>). It expanded its operations through the Society's grant programme. [Gewape Cloud Group says on its own LinkedIn account that it is connected and live on RINEX, run by RICTA](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/gewape-cloud-group_gewapecloud-rinex-rwandacloud-activity-7468194906369593344-ao9G>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found gives RINEX's members or says a global content network has a cache there or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[Internet Society Pulse, from PeeringDB data of August 2026, shows SIXP Sudan (Sudan Internet Exchange Point) with four members at 1 Gbps each](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/ixp-tracker/ixp/660/>). [PeeringDB's record, operated by the National Information Center of Sudan in Khartoum, shows 4 peers and 4G total capacity, last updated 2020-01-22](<https://www.peeringdb.com/ix/2320>). [The Center's WSIS Forum 2016 deck lists a National Internet Exchange Point among its services](<https://www.itu.int/net4/wsis/forum/2016/Content/AgendaFiles/document/14d93639-cc47-4322-b464-5d97518a6653/NIC_SUDAN.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[In September 2026 the Internet Society's IXP Tracker listed HubSIX, an exchange point in Dakar, with six member networks](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/ixp-tracker/ixp/1594/>), five of them at the route server. They have 260 Gbps of port capacity between them. In the last twelve months, a second exchange opened in Dakar. [the African IXP Association lists SENIX, opened in 2017, and HubSIX, opened in 2026](<https://af-ix.org/ixps-list>). No source found says a global content network serves from either exchange. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[PeeringDB's record for Michcom-IX, an open-access exchange in Freetown run by Michcom Limited, lists 5 peers, 6 connections and 60G total capacity, last updated 2026-06-03](<https://www.peeringdb.com/ix/4892>). [The operator's own site says a Microsoft Connected Cache node caches Microsoft content locally at the exchange](<https://www.michcom-ix.net/>). It also says operators across Sierra Leone, Guinea and Liberia exchange traffic there, with points of presence in Conakry and Monrovia. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found gives the exchange's traffic at two dates a year apart. Operating would need traffic figures at two dates a year or more apart, the later higher.

[Packet Clearing House's directory lists the Somali Internet Exchange Point (SoIXP) in Mogadishu, run by the National Communications Authority Somalia and established 20 November 2018, with status Active](<https://www.pch.net/ixp/details/2072>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names the exchange's members or gives its traffic. None says a global content network has a cache at the exchange or peers there, and none names a second city. Establishing would need a global content network, such as Google or Meta, to have a cache there or peer there.

[In July 2025 Internet Society Pulse's Internet Resilience Index, from PCH and PeeringDB data, scored South Sudan 0/100 on IXP coverage of population centres](<https://pulse.internetsociety.org/en/resilience/ss/>). It also scored 0/100 on peering efficiency, the share of networks peering at an IXP. Nothing dated later names an exchange in service. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need an exchange point in service, where networks hand each other traffic directly, whoever runs it.

[In November 2025 Teraco said 680 networks peer at NAPAfrica](<https://www.teraco.co.za/news/napafrica-and-teraco-acx-growing-africas-digital-community-as-napafrica-hits-6tbps/>), among them Akamai, Cloudflare, Google, Meta, Netflix and TikTok. [Teraco gives its traffic peak as over 4 Tbps in 2023 and 5 Tbps in February 2025](<https://www.teraco.co.za/news/napafrica-internet-exchange-achieves-5tbps-traffic-milestone-driving-africas-digital-transformation/>). Its members come from over 50 countries. In the last twelve months, [NAPAfrica reached 6 Tbps in November 2025](<https://www.teraco.co.za/news/napafrica-and-teraco-acx-growing-africas-digital-community-as-napafrica-hits-6tbps/>), and [over 7 Tbps with more than 690 networks in November 2026](<https://www.mybroadband.co.za/news/cloud-hosting/678481-south-africas-biggest-internet-exchange-point-hits-7tbps-and-gets-800gbps-ports.html>).
